title: Ethiopia Government Relations and Program Support Coordinator (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role Seeking a Government Relations & Program Support Coordinator to liaise with Zonal/Woreda offices, support program growth in North Shewa zone, strengthen partnerships, ensure compliance, de-risk fieldwork, and travel frequently. The duty station will be at Debre Berhan Town ). Responsibilities Manage work relationships with woreda government and Zonal Focal Persons (FPs) Serve as the primary day-to-day liaison with woreda and zonal project focal persons (FP) and other government stakeholders. Proactively identify government relations issues at the woreda and kebele levels by maintaining close communication with the program team, particularly Tree Officers (TOs) and Cluster Leads (CLs), and work with relevant government stakeholders to resolve them in a timely manner. Participate in the weekly cluster lead meetings to understand GR challenges that may exist in the field and resolve them on time by leveraging run alignment meetings with woreda and zonal FPs as needed Attend other government meetings as directed by the Senior Partnerships Associate Update contacts and meeting notes on Customer Relationship Management tool Leverage networks and knowledge of the landscape to help identify opportunities to expand and/or improve One Acre Fund’s work Prepare, organize, review, and Submit documents as required on time to project signatory offices and other government offices, especially quarterly reports Gather inputs for quarterly reports from department leads or their designee Write and develop clear and concise quarterly reports that track progress and inform project stakeholders. Coordinate the review from his manager, incorporate comments, and finalize the report. Coordinate the submission of the reports to the woreda and zonal project signatory offices. Prepare project mid-term and terminal reports. Prepare outgoing letters for woredas as needed. Identify, monitor, and obtain all compliance requirements at the woreda and zonal government level and submit documents as required. Track woreda FPs’ and DAs’ support to OAF activities and field staff on a weekly basis, evaluate results, and take appropriate actions to increase program efficiency Monitor the assistance provided by woreda FPs and DAs to OAF operations on a weekly basis using a tracker Evaluate results and resolve issues in consultation with Woreda SHs and zonal focal persons. Ensure that the woreda FPs and DAs are fulfilling their roles and responsibilities as per prior agreements with One Acre Fund Follow up and ensure the woreda office of agriculture takes appropriate actions on the focal persons and DAs with underperformance issues. Participate in the resolution of identified issues/risks with manager support. Troubleshooting of Woreda Government Relations in consultation with the Senior Partnerships Specialist and with escalation, Organize and lead meetings and trainings as needed with support from your manager Provide GR capacity-building trainings to field team at least once a year Support on GR orientation and onboarding of new Woreda and Kebele employees, Co-lead project launch, mid-term, and terminal workshops Support/facilitate field visits and events for external stakeholders. Provide other administrative support as needed Other Projects Other Partnerships and Program projects as assigned by your supervisor (when time and skill allow) Special projects are the key to growth at OAF, and we want someone who is excited to grow their responsibilities through projects outside of their core responsibilities. Special projects in the first year might include things like data entry, translating documents into Amharic, scanning and binding of documents, support on inventory, support during input distributions, and support during seedling distribution. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Required Qualifications—these will be verified and tested during the selection process University degree Minimum three years of work experience At least one year of partnerships or communications work experience Worked and lived in the North Shewa Zone for at least two years Experience in Independently facilitating and organizing workshops Some public speaking or training delivery or teaching experience Very good report writing, communication and interpersonal skills Excellent attention to details Willingness to travel to rural kebeles using public transport Professional and formal demeanor Good problem-solving skills and ability to learn quickly Challenge anticipation skills Good computer skills—in email, Excel and Word Fluent in English, Amharic (both written and spoken) Preferred Qualifications University Degree in a related subject (Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Communication, Management, Law, etc.) Experience working in the agriculture sector, particularly within the agricultural extension system or in natural resource management (NRM). Experience managing projects and/or teams. Experience designing, implementing, or coordinating agricultural pilot projects or field trials. Experience working within or closely with government institutions. Demonstrated experience collaborating with multiple stakeholders, including government agencies, NGOs, community organizations, and development partners. Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Debre Berhan, Amhara, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia. Application Deadline 27 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

title: Physiotherapist
description:
The Physiotherapist is responsible for the treatment, counselling, preventative care and rehabilitation of the motor function and physical wellness of the patients. is responsible for assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating individualized rehabilitation programs for patients with limb loss and other mobility impairments. Working within a multidisciplinary team, the Physiotherapist facilitates functional recovery, promotes independence, optimizes prosthetic use, and improves patients’ quality of life through evidence-based rehabilitation practices The Physiotherapist tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following points: Undertake a comprehensive and accurate assessment of patients in a variety of settings; Identify, plan and manage physiotherapy interventions and rehabilitation plans Provide physio treatments to achieve identified outcomes and monitor patients’ conditions, both for in-patients and out-patients, if needed; Perform all the tasks related to the physio competence framework; Establish, maintain and conclude therapeutic interpersonal relationships with patients and their relatives, based on respect, dignity and care; Conduct comprehensive physical assessments of patients with upper and lower limb amputations, including musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, balance, gait, and functional evaluations. Provide pre-prosthetic rehabilitation, including: residual limb care and shaping, edema management, scar management, pain management (including phantom limb pain where appropriate), range of motion and strengthening exercises, contracture prevention Cardiovascular conditioning Deliver prosthetic rehabilitation, including: prosthetic gait training, balance and coordination training, functional mobility training Stair negotiation and community ambulation Transfers and activities of daily living (ADL) training Fall prevention strategies Monitor patient progress and modify treatment plans according to clinical outcomes. Encourage patients to have a positive attitude towards physiotherapy by motivating them; Organizing daily group activities, if possible, for patients; Promote an environment that enables patient’s safety and health implementing all necessary actions such as infection control practices, bed sores prevention practices and maintaining high level of hygiene also ensuring physio material are properly cleaned; Ensure that the equipment is functional and well maintained and stored; Ensure documentation/record is accurate and physio chart is properly filled, maintaining confidentially of information; Compiling and submitting periodic reports, if requested, following EMERGENCY guidelines; Be compliant with EMERGENCY guidelines for the treatment of patients; Work closely with prosthetists/orthotists during prosthetic prescription, fitting, alignment, and follow-up. Provide clinical feedback regarding prosthetic fit, function, comfort, and patient performance. Participate in training programs or activities, meeting timelines and deliverables, if requested by EMERGENCY; Train new staff, if needed. Job requirements: Degree in the Physio field; (Bachelor’s Degree in Physiotherapy from a recognized institution). Postgraduate training in rehabilitation, prosthetics, amputee rehabilitation, or neurorehabilitation Experience working in prosthetic and orthotic services. Good problem solving, time management and technical skills and willingness to learn new procedures and techniques; Good communication, interpersonal skills and high level of empathy, patience and ability to handle emotional and pressure situations; Basic Computer Skills, including Microsoft Office Program; Good level of English, written and spoken.

How to Apply: Send your application at this link: [EMERGENCY NGO](https://emergency-hq.orangehrmlive.com/external/#/recruitment-apply/vacancy/166)

title: Mine Action Specialist
description:
Overview of position General Background Our client supports the successful implementation of its partners’ peacebuilding, humanitarian and development projects around the world. Our mission is to serve people in need by expanding the ability of the United Nations, governments and other partners to manage projects, infrastructure and procurement in a sustainable and efficient manner. Working in some of the world’s most challenging environments, our vision is to advance sustainable implementation practices, always satisfying or surpassing our partners’ expectations. With over 7,000 personnel spread across 80 countries, our client offers its partners the logistical, technical and management knowledge they need, wherever they need it. A flexible structure and global reach mean that we can quickly respond to our partners' needs, while offering the benefits of economies of scale. Please provide general background information on the context of the engagement. Background Information - Peace and Security Cluster For over 20 years, our clients Peace and Security Cluster (PSC) has served as a key implementation platform supporting the work of its largest partner. Through a strategic partnership, PSC delivers interlinked portfolio, programme and project management services, reinforced by robust oversight and risk management controls tailored to operations in complex and high-risk environments. Operating under the leadership of the Cluster Director - who holds overall authority and accountability for PSC’s performance on behalf of its clients - the Cluster provides day-to-day management of their partners field programmes. This includes comprehensive support across human resources, procurement, contract management, planning, implementation, and financial oversight, ensuring full compliance with our client rules and regulations and donor requirements. PSC’s service delivery is complemented by cross-cutting initiatives, including knowledge and information management, gender equality, diversity and inclusion and quality assurance. The Cluster enables agile deployment and operational flexibility, allowing field programmes to respond swiftly to shifting needs in dynamic operational contexts. It also plays an essential role in donor reporting and visibility, ensuring that funding is used transparently and effectively. Background Information Established in 1997, our clients partner works to eliminate the threat of landmines, explosive remnants of war (ERW), and improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Their partner leads operational responses, coordinates mine action across the UN system, and contributes to global standards and policy development. They supports the UN's vision of "a world free of the threat of landmines and unexploded ordnance, where individuals and communities live in a safe environment conducive to development, and where mine survivors are fully integrated into their societies." Operating under mandates from both the UN General Assembly and Security Council, their functions as a specialized service within the Department of Peace Operations (DPO). They operates under UN legislative mandates of both the General Assembly and the Security Council, or at the request of the UN Secretary-General or his designated official. When instructed by the Security Council or called upon by Member States, their partner deploys under humanitarian, peace and security mandates. Their main headquarters is in the UN Secretariat, New York with a sub-office in Geneva. They provides direct support and assistance in the areas of explosive hazard threat mitigation to 18 countries/territories/missions, has a standby rapid response capacity and global technical advisors in the field of IEDs and Weapons and Ammunition Management. As an office within DPO, their partner supports peacekeeping and special political missions in accordance with Security Council mandates. They chair the Inter-Agency Coordination Group on Mine Action (IACG-MA) and leads the Mine Action Area of Responsibility under the Global Protection Cluster. It also chairs the IMAS Review Board and leads the UN Coordinating Task Force on IEDs, supporting the Secretary-General’s Disarmament Agenda. Background Information - Sudan The Sudan Programme, based in Port Sudan, works in close coordination with the National Mine Action Authority (NMAA), the UN Country Team and humanitarian partners. The project aims to protect civilians from the threat of explosive ordnance (EO) and strengthen the resilience of conflict-affected communities through a comprehensive, gender-mainstreamed and conflict-sensitive mine action response. It also supports broader humanitarian, early recovery and stabilization efforts by enabling safe access to areas contaminated by EO. Their Sudan’s key activities include land release operations, including urban EOD activities and building clearance, with the operational focus expected to shift toward the clearance of AT mines, including minimum-metal variants; delivery of both direct and indirect Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), tailored to different gender and age groups; and provision of technical advice to humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding (HDP) actors to help them safely operate in EO-affected environments. The project also leads the coordination of the Mine Action Area of Responsibility (MA AoR) in Sudan, co-chairing the sector under the Global Protection Cluster framework. Through this role, their partner ensures that mine action is effectively integrated into humanitarian coordination mechanisms and that EO threats are adequately understood and addressed at all levels. While the Programme’s current operational footprint is primarily focused on areas under the control of the Sudan Government - especially urban areas in Khartoum and Al Jazirah - Sudan aspires to expand its outreach to all EO-affected regions, addressing both legacy contamination and new threats emerging from the ongoing conflict. Role objectives Under the direct supervision of the Head of Project Unit / Chief of Operations (HPU/CoO) or its representative, the Mine Action Specialist will perform the following tasks: Operations – Design and planning Support in providing input to the HPU or its representative on programme and project design documents from an operational and technical standpoint, such as: Workplan (e.g., nature of the threat, technical personnel and equipment requirements, etc.) Concept of Operations Input into the documents above is from the operational and technical aspects encompassing mine action pillars (e.g., clearance, explosive ordnance disposal, explosive ordnance risk education, victim assistance, advocacy, and stockpile destruction) Ensure that implementation plans have viable timelines, are assigned appropriate resources, and that implementation options reflect the knowledge of the context, as well as mechanisms and policies; key implementation documents include: Our clients Project Agreements Solicitation documents used to contract third parties (i.e., contractors and grantees) Human resources plan Support the design and planning of the national concept of operations and workplan, providing technical input to help ensure alignment with applicable standards, priorities and operational requirements. Operations - Implementation and monitoring Support and participate in the technical reviews to ensure operations are conducted in accordance with our clients policies and both International and National Mine Action standards, such as: Project management standards, Health, safety, social and environmental standards, Gender parity and mainstreaming policies, Ethics and standards of conduct, Information management systems and standards and Organizational design standards and human resources policies; Where applicable, in collaboration with the NMAC and as tasked, conduct routine on-site QA of Mine Action Organization operations (for monitoring and post-clearance inspections) and as part of the Accreditation process to ensure operations are conducted in accordance with mine action technical standards, such as: International and National Mine Action Standards (IMAS) and corresponding National Technical Specifications and Guidelines (NTSGs); Oversee, coordinate, and monitor mine action operations and performance (both operations conducted in-house and those conducted through third-party contractors and grantees). Ensure third-party contracts and grants are delivered in accordance with mine action technical, operational and quality assurance processes (Implementation Plan, SOPs, task orders issuance, accreditation). Implement the program quality management and information management system. Familiarize with and, when required, deliver EO-related courses, including SSAFE. Advise the HPU or its representative and the NMAC CoO on potential technical and operational issues that may impact the achievement of programme/project outcomes and appropriate solutions. Ensure operational plans are updated and reviewed regularly. Monitor and react to emerging trends in Land Release activities. Capacity Building & Mentorship Act as a mentor and training officer for the NMAC, providing guidance and support in operational implementation, operations management and field-level programme delivery in line with the NMAC-established priorities Develop training plans in conjunction with the HPU / CoO based on NMAC and MA Programme requirements and deliver training courses as necessary or when requested by the NMAC. description:
